intent: Customer asks whether she should return an unexpected £750 credit by paying it to a different account supplied in a text message from an unknown number.
summary: Decline any customer-initiated return of the £750 to the texted details: they differ from the originating account, Confirmation of Payee returned ANNM (name does not match), the text came from an unknown mobile, and no recovery request has been received from Meridian Bank. Escalate urgently to the fraud/security team as a suspected mistaken-payment redirect scam, passing full payment/text details and the unresolved OCR-vs-record discrepancy. Tell the customer not to send anything, to leave the £750 untouched, and that a genuine return comes via the payer's own bank's recovery process.

facts.claim: A Faster Payment of £750.00 from "R JAMES" (Meridian Bank, sort code SYN-SC-06-2, account SYN-ACCT-06-2), reference "RENT", end-to-end ID MER26092622143198, was credited to the customer's account on 2026-09-26 at 22:14:31+01:00.
No inbound funds-recovery request has been received from Meridian Bank for this payment.
The customer received a text on Sun 27 Sep 08:41 from +44 7700 900 823, signed "Ryan", asking her to send the £750 to a different ("other") account rather than the one it came from.

The case record states the text supplied SYN-SC-06-3 / SYN-ACCT-06-1 and the customer states these differ from the originating account; the machine OCR transcript instead reads SYN-SC-06-2 / SYN-ACCT-06-2 (the originating account). This discrepancy is unresolved; the original image was not read.

A Confirmation of Payee check on the details given in the text (SYN-SC-06-3 / SYN-ACCT-06-1, name "R James", personal) returned no match, reason ANNM "Account name does not match", at 2026-09-28T09:52:40Z.
The customer states she has not touched the funds and wants to return them; she is a 20-year-old student account holder with typical low-value activity.
The customer is contacting the bank through in-app personal banking chat.

missing: Whether Meridian Bank will raise a formal funds-recovery request for end-to-end ID MER26092622143198 (none received at decision time)

The exact sort code/account number in the text: case record and customer say a different account (SYN-SC-06-3 / SYN-ACCT-06-1) while the OCR transcript reads SYN-SC-06-2 / SYN-ACCT-06-2; original image unread
Fraud/security team assessment of the inbound credit and whether they choose to ring-fence the £750 or contact Meridian
Whether the sender of the text is the genuine payer (not verifiable from supplied evidence)

steps.instruction: Decline to initiate, assist or recommend any outbound payment of the £750.00 credit (end-to-end ID MER26092622143198) to the details supplied in the 27 Sep text (recorded as SYN-SC-06-3 / SYN-ACCT-06-1, name 'R James'). Reason: the details differ from the originating Meridian account SYN-SC-06-2 / SYN-ACCT-06-2, Confirmation of Payee returned ANNM (name does not match), the request came from an unknown mobile number, and no funds-recovery request has been received from Meridian Bank. Scope: the customer-initiated return only; no other account activity is restricted by this step.

rationale.explanation: A request to return a 'mistaken' credit to a different account than it came from, backed by a CoP no-match and with no recovery request from the sending bank, is concrete warning evidence; the risky action is the customer sending the money herself.
rationale.criterion: Treat a pressured redirect request with CoP mismatch as warning evidence; stop the risky proposed action and specify what is on hold.

steps.instruction: Escalate urgently to the Harrow & Vale Bank fraud/security team as a suspected mistaken-payment redirect scam. Pass: customer Aisha Khan (student current account); inbound FPS £750.00 GBP received 2026-09-26T22:14:31+01:00 from 'R JAMES', Meridian Bank, SYN-SC-06-2 / SYN-ACCT-06-2, ref 'RENT', end-to-end ID MER26092622143198, recovery_request_received=false; text received Sun 27 Sep 08:41 from +44 7700 900 823 signed 'Ryan' asking for payment to an 'other' account; CoP on texted details SYN-SC-06-3 / SYN-ACCT-06-1 'R James' = ANNM at 2026-09-28T09:52:40Z; unresolved discrepancy between the case record (SYN-SC-06-3 / SYN-ACCT-06-1) and the OCR transcript (SYN-SC-06-2 / SYN-ACCT-06-2) — original screenshot attached for their review; customer has not spent the funds and has not yet made any payment. Ask the team to review the inbound credit, decide whether to ring-fence the £750 pending any Meridian recovery request, and handle any liaison with Meridian Bank.

rationale.explanation: The pattern (unexpected credit, unknown-number text, redirect to a different account, CoP mismatch, no sending-bank recovery request) warrants an urgent fraud handoff with all identifiers so the team can protect the customer and resolve the account-detail discrepancy from the original image.
rationale.criterion: Suspected scam in progress requires hold of the risky action plus urgent fraud/security escalation; name an unresolved record conflict rather than guessing.

steps.instruction: Reply in the in-app chat: 'Yes, that is a problem, and you've done exactly the right thing by asking first. Please don't send the £750 yourself, and don't reply to the text. The account in the text is different from the one the money actually came from, and when we checked the details in the text, the name "R James" does not match the account they gave you. We also haven't received any request from the sender's bank to recover the payment, so we can't confirm the person texting is the real sender. If this really was a mistake, the right way to fix it is for the sender to contact their own bank (Meridian Bank), which can send us a formal recovery request — we then return it through that process, and you don't need to make a payment yourself. In the meantime please leave the £750 untouched in your account and keep the text message. I've referred this to our fraud team to review; that doesn't mean it's definitely a scam, and it doesn't mean the money has been recalled yet — I can't give you a timescale for that. Any genuine contact from us will come through the app or our published numbers, and we will never ask for your PIN, password or one-time codes.'

rationale.explanation: Answers the customer's direct question with the recorded facts (different account, CoP no match, no recovery request), gives the supported route for a genuine return, and states what the referral does not confirm.
rationale.criterion: Reply with the recorded status and what it does not confirm; never facilitate a transfer to the suspected party; do not promise recall or reimbursement outcomes.

must_state: Do not send the £750 yourself to the details in the text, and do not reply to or act on the text
The account details in the text are different from the account the money came from, and our Confirmation of Payee check shows the name 'R James' does not match the account named in the text
We cannot confirm that the person texting is the real sender of the payment
The proper route for a genuine mistaken payment is for the payer to contact their own bank (Meridian Bank), which can send us a formal recovery request; we will then deal with it through that process
Please leave the £750 untouched in your account in the meantime and keep the text message
We have referred this to our fraud team for review; this does not confirm it is fraud and does not mean the money has been recalled yet
Any genuine contact about this from us will come through the app or our published contact numbers; we will never ask for your PIN, password or one-time codes
must_not: Do not tell or allow the customer to transfer the funds to the texted details or to any account supplied by the texter
Do not state as fact that the texter is a scammer or that the payer's account is compromised
Do not promise that Meridian will recall the payment, any timescale, or that the customer will be protected from loss
Do not ask the customer for PINs, passwords or one-time codes
Do not disclose the payer's account details beyond what the customer already holds
Do not describe the fraud referral as completed or as having produced an outcome
